messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED (SEV2) — 1879991111
incident-bot: Elevated misroute rate observed between eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Symptom: requests intended for 'redwood-llm-v2' are being routed to an older quantized fallback model leading to garbled outputs and higher error rates. Auto-escalating to #incidents. Pager: @oncall-ml.
oncall-ml: ack. I'm looking at the routing logs. First pass: looks like fallback weight suddenly increased around 1879991098. Taking lead.
sre_jane: Oncall, can you confirm customer impact (error counts, affected customers)? I'll stand up deeper trace.
oncall-ml: quick numbers: -> 2k failing requests/min at peak. Top 3 affected customers: acme-corp, neat-app, docu-flow. Roughly 15% request latency > 3s, 9% malformed outputs.
eng_tom: I can flip routing policy if we confirm it's policy churn. Any recent deploys to routing-controller? infra_eli?
infra_eli: No deploys in the last 12h from infra side. Autoscaler did trigger extra instances in us-west-2 at 1879991060.
ops-bot: Deploybot: routing-controller v1.43 was promoted at 1879990712 by ci-bot. No hotfix since.
sre_jane: pulling sample logs now. Sharing tail from router (filtered):
```
[1879991089] route_eval client=acme-corp route_priority=cost score=0.42 selected=fallback-llm-q8b
[1879991095] route_eval client=neat-app route_priority=latency score=0.91 selected=fallback-llm-q8b
[1879991102] model_proxy failed_decode model=fallback-llm-q8b err=kv-cache-mismatch
[1879991107] routing: fallback_count++ reason=capacity_constrained region=eu-west-1
```
eng_tom: kv-cache-mismatch on the quantized fallback sounds like incompatible KV format between model variants. That explains malformed outputs.
oncall-ml: hypothesis 1: traffic spike caused primary pool to saturate -> smart-routing incorrectly preferred a smaller quantized fallback that doesn't share KV format -> misdecode. Hypothesis 2: misconfiguration bumped fallback_priority to higher weight for some customers. Need to test weight history and recent policy changes.
product-ana: FYI, a customer support case just popped for acme-corp around 1879991118. They reported hallucinated responses.
sre_jane: I'm running a route-policy diff for the last 24h. Sharing snippet:
```
--- policy@1879900000
+++ policy@1879991000
@@ -42,7 +42,7 @@
   - name: primary-llm
     weight: 0.95
-  - name: fallback-llm-q8b
-    weight: 0.05
+  - name: fallback-llm-q8b
+    weight: 0.30
```
sre_jane: Looks like an automated rebalancer temporarily increased fallback weight from 5% to 30% to relieve overloaded nodes. It aligns with the autoscaler.
infra_eli: Rebalancer job id rjob-5589 ran at 1879991055 due to cluster pressure. It adjusted weights per policy-compute.
eng_tom: mitigation proposal: set fallback weight back to 0.05 and/or exclude clients with strict model compatibility from being eligible for fallback. I can push a hotfix to route-controller, small change.
oncall-ml: do it. Also, can we throttle or pause the rebalancer while we stabilize?
infra_eli: pausing rebalancer now. Command: `rjob pause rjob-5589` -> accepted at 1879991132.
eng_tom: pushing policy rollback now: `policy apply --set fallback-llm-q8b.weight=0.05 --dry-run=false` -> pushed at 1879991140.
ops-bot: Policy change deployed (id=pc-1879991140) by eng_tom.
eng_tom: confirming route evals after change:
```
[1879991152] route_eval client=acme-corp selected=primary-llm
[1879991153] route_eval client=neat-app selected=primary-llm
```
oncall-ml: early signal: error rate dropping. From 2k/min down to ~140/min. Latency tail improving. Holding until stable.
product-ana: customer notifications: sending a short note to the affected accounts. cc: support.
sre_jane: collecting traces for RCA. Need full model_proxy logs and KV cache mismatches. Request to eng-runtime for model artifact compatibility matrix.
eng_tom: attaching quick dump of model metadata for both variants (trimmed):
```
primary-llm-v2: kv_format=v2, vocab=bytess, kv_epoch=7
fallback-llm-q8b: kv_format=v1, vocab=bytess, kv_epoch=4\```
eng_tom: mismatch confirmed — fallback uses older kv_format. So when router redirects live sessions mid-conversation, model_proxy attempts to reuse KV cache and fails -> garbled outputs.
sre_jane: timeline draft (will be refined):
T+ -00:10   1879991010  small cluster pressure starts (normal ramp)
T+ -00:05   1879991055  rebalancer rjob-5589 increases fallback weight to 30%
T+ +00:00   1879991089  routing selects fallback increasingly; malformed outputs start
T+ +00:07   1879991140  policy rollback applied to fallback weight 5%
T+ +00:12   1879991165  error rate drops to baseline

noncall-ml: action items (short term):
- eng_tom: ensure policy rollback is persisted and add per-client exclusion rules (owner).
- eng-runtime: produce compatibility matrix and add guard in router for kv_format mismatch (owner: eng_runtime_team).
- infra_eli: audit rebalancer heuristics to avoid directing stateful sessions to incompatible fallbacks (owner).
- product-ana: coordinate customer comms and incident page (owner).

eng_tom: I created a short-term guard: route-controller will now check model.kv_format equality before issuing fallback for ongoing sessions. Deployed feature flag at 1879991188 (ff=guard-kv-eq).
ops-bot: Featureflagbot: flag guard-kv-eq enabled in prod at 1879991188.
sre_jane: confirming metrics: by 1879991200 malformed output rate < 0.5%. Good.
product-ana: drafting post-incident message. Will include apology + mitigation steps.
eng_tom: for RCA: root cause = rebalancer increased fallback weight to relieve capacity, but fallback model was incompatible (kv_format mismatch) and router lacked guard to prevent stateful session migration -> misroutes and malformed outputs.
infra_eli: note: autoscaler + rebalancer decisions are orthogonal; we need coordinated policy that understands stateful workloads. Adding as infra backlog item.
sre_jane: tagging follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-142 (kv compatibility checks), ROUTING-218 (per-client fallback exclusion), INFRA-990 (rebalancer policy review), DOCS-55 (support runbook updates).
oncall-ml: closing on-call; handing to eng_tom for RCA writeup. I'll monitor for another 30m.
eng_tom: taking RCA. I'll assemble timeline + logs and post in #postmortems. Assigning draft due EOD.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. SEV2 -> postmortem required.
sre_jane: quick note: no data exfiltration or PII exposure suspected. All affected responses were malformed, not leaking unrelated content.
product-ana: thanks all. If anything else crops up ping me.
ops-bot: Incident closed oncall handoff at 1879992022.
